dz.headline: Algerian security seizes 10.4 million pregabalin capsules
dz.body: Police seized 10.4 million pregabalin capsules and more than 33 kg of cocaine in a major operation. The National Security agency reported the haul followed the dismantling of an international criminal network.
dz.why: The operation disrupts the supply chain of psychotropic substances and narcotics for drug traffickers.

dz.headline: STI opens smartphone plant in Oran to produce 6,000 units daily
dz.body: A new smartphone assembly plant by STI, in partnership with China's vivo, aims to produce 6,000 phones per day at maximum capacity. The 7,000-square-meter facility currently employs approximately 200 workers.
dz.why: Local assembly increases the availability of vivo brand devices and creates 200 industrial jobs in the Sania industrial zone.

dz.headline: Algerian government targets 20,000 investment projects by 2029
dz.body: The government set a goal to realize 20,000 investment projects by 2029. The plan relies on a comprehensive census of available land.
dz.why: The initiative seeks to expand the national industrial base by increasing the amount of land available for corporate development.

dz.headline: ONAB sells frozen chicken at 350 dinars per kilogram
dz.body: The National Office of Livestock Feed (ONAB) is selling frozen chicken at 350 dinars per kg across 143 points of sale. The agency's general administration director said supplies are being released gradually on a daily basis.
dz.why: The fixed pricing provides a lower-cost protein alternative for consumers across various provinces.

dz.headline: Algeria adds 6 digital services to government portal
dz.body: The High Commissariat for Digitization introduced six new digital services to the national government portal. These services, developed with the Ministry of Energy and Renewable Energies, include the E-SANED platform for processing production facility licenses.
dz.why: Energy companies can now apply for exploitation licenses and declarations electronically rather than through manual filings.

ao.headline: Angola expels 53,000 irregular foreigners over seven months
ao.body: Angolan police deported more than 53,000 foreign citizens in irregular situations over the last seven months. Commissioner Francisco Ribas announced the figures following a National Security Council meeting in Luanda. Many of those expelled were allegedly involved in the illicit exploitation of diamonds.
ao.why: The operational plan aims to reduce illegal immigration and curb the theft of national mineral resources.

ao.headline: Unitel restores national communications after three-week outage
ao.body: Unitel has completed the restoration of voice, messaging, data, and internet services across Angola. The company stated in a market communiqué that the outage lasted more than three weeks and was caused by a cyberattack. Call-waiting services remain offline until a future date.
ao.why: The restoration returns mobile and internet connectivity to users and third-party services operating on the network.

ao.headline: UNITA files criminal complaint against Uíge governor and police
ao.body: The opposition party UNITA filed a criminal complaint against Uíge Governor José Carvalho da Rocha and police leadership. Vice-president Arlete Chimbinda announced the move during a press conference. The complaint follows attacks on party militants on August 8.
ao.why: The legal action seeks accountability for violence directed at opposition members in the Uíge province.

ao.headline: MPLA presidential hopeful Higino Carneiro refuses to withdraw
ao.body: General Higino Carneiro stated he will not exit the race for the leadership of the MPLA. He spoke to journalists after a Supreme Court session in Luanda. Carneiro is currently contesting charges of embezzlement and money laundering.
ao.why: The general's persistence maintains a challenge to the leadership of the party that has held power for 50 years.

ao.headline: William Tonet robbed in Morro Bento
ao.body: Director William Tonet was the victim of a qualified robbery on August 19 at 9:20 p.m. The incident occurred in a side street in Morro Bento while Tonet was visiting a clinic. The Dic-Samba picket registered the case.
ao.why: The robbery occurred after Tonet had reportedly rejected police escorts provided by the CNE.

bj.headline: Benin releases cyberactivist Steve Amoussou
bj.body: Beninese cyberactivist Steve Amoussou has been released from custody. Amoussou, known as the chronicler "Frère Hounvi," was prosecuted by the CRIET for publications critical of the authorities.
bj.why: The release ends the detention of a critic who had been arrested in Lomé on August 12, 2024, and transferred to Cotonou.

bj.headline: Benin health ministry releases recruitment results August 20
bj.body: Recruitment test results for health agents at departmental health directorates are available Thursday, August 20, 2026. The results were issued by the ministry of health.
bj.why: The publication of these lists allows selected candidates to begin their appointments to health structures.

bj.headline: Benin Sports Minister visits U20 women's team in France
bj.body: Minister of Sports and Civic Engagement Benoît Dato visited the U20 women's national team on August 18, 2026. The team is currently in a training camp in France.
bj.why: The visit serves as preparation for the team's participation in the FIFA U20 Women's World Cup Poland 2026, starting in two weeks.

bj.headline: Djougou hosts 25th national primary school championships
bj.body: The 25th edition of the national primary school championships began on August 17, 2026, in Djougou. The event is organized by the Union of Sports and Cultural Associations of Primary Education (UASCEP).
bj.why: The four-day competition brings together young athletes from all departments of Benin to compete in sports and cultural events.

bj.headline: LNB S.A. launches 'Super Amazone' scratch ticket for 200 FCFA
bj.body: LNB S.A. has released a new scratch ticket called 'Super Amazone' priced at 200 FCFA. The ticket offers prizes of up to 1,000,000 FCFA.
bj.why: The new product allows consumers to gamble for a maximum prize of 1 million FCFA using a themed ticket.

bw.headline: Botswana inflation falls to 9.4% in July
bw.body: Annual inflation decreased to 9.4% in July from 10.7% in June. Statistics Botswana attributed the 1.3 percentage-point decline to a 6.5% drop in the transport index.
bw.why: Lower fuel prices reduced transport costs for consumers and businesses after a price surge earlier this year.

bw.headline: MMG finds 1.4 million tonnes of copper at Khoemacau mine
bw.body: MMG Ltd discovered a new copper-silver deposit containing an estimated 1.4 million tonnes of copper and 90 million ounces of silver. The Kgwebe deposit is located approximately six kilometers from the existing Zone 5 mine.
bw.why: The discovery increases the long-term mineral resources and growth prospects for the Khoemacau operation.

bw.headline: Botswana retains P1,500 daily per diem for public servants
bw.body: The government maintained a P1,500 daily local per diem for public servants, according to the Hospitality and Tourism Association of Botswana. Starting Sept. 1, 2026, officials must provide receipts for accommodation components up to P900.
bw.why: The policy is expected to increase demand for the domestic hospitality industry.

bw.headline: African Development Bank values Botswana natural capital at $116 billion
bw.body: The African Development Bank estimated Botswana's natural capital, including wildlife and water, at $116 billion as of 2020. The figure represents the value of assets over time rather than liquid funds for spending.
bw.why: The government is looking to these assets as alternative sources of growth and financing to reduce dependence on diamonds.

bw.headline: Botswana working-age population to reach 67.6% by 2038
bw.body: The population of people aged 15 to 64 is projected to rise to 67.6% by 2038. The Sunday Standard reports this demographic shift creates a potential economic dividend.
bw.why: The country must now increase productivity and generate more jobs to prevent the expanding workforce from becoming an economic burden.

bf.headline: ANEVE cuts environmental permit processing from 126 to 26 days
bf.body: The National Agency for Environmental Evaluations (ANEVE) reduced dossier processing times from 126 days to 26 days. The agency announced the reform during a meeting with approved environmental and social evaluation firms on Aug. 20.
bf.why: The shorter approval window allows businesses to begin construction or operations on new projects faster.

bf.headline: Tour du Faso 2026 sets 600 million FCFA budget
bf.body: The 37th edition of the Tour du Faso will run from Oct. 30 to Nov. 8 with a projected budget of 600 million FCFA. Minister of Sports Annick Pikbougoum Zingué Ouattara detailed the figures during a meeting with sponsors and partners on Aug. 20.
bf.why: The event requires increased mobilization of corporate partners to fund the cycling competition's operational costs.

bf.headline: Police intercept 7 minors headed for gold mines
bf.body: The Regional Brigade for Child Protection (BRPE) intercepted seven minors, the eldest aged 12, on Aug. 18. The children were stopped in Koudougou while traveling to artisanal gold mining sites.
bf.why: The operation prevents children from entering hazardous labor conditions at gold mining sites.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso Foreign Minister meets UN special envoy
bf.body: Foreign Minister Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré received UN Special Envoy Sahle-Work Zewde on Aug. 20. Zewde is visiting to evaluate the actions of the UN Regional Office for West Africa and the Sahel (UNOWAS).
bf.why: The mission assesses the effectiveness of UN regional oversight and diplomatic coordination in the Sahel.

bf.headline: AS Police trains 110 female players in Ouagadougou
bf.body: The AS Police sports association is conducting a training workshop for 110 young female players from various clubs from Aug. 20 to 21. The program focuses on female empowerment through football.
bf.why: The training provides young women with professional sports skills and tools for social autonomy.

bi.headline: Beer prices in Gitega double official rates
bi.body: Primus and Amstel beers are selling at twice the official price in Gitega. Iwacu reports the price spikes follow Brarudi's decision to export products to the DRC to offset a lack of foreign currency.
bi.why: Consumers in Gitega now face inflated costs for beverages due to generalized market speculation.

bi.headline: Gitega installs first functional medical scanner outside Bujumbura
bi.body: A medical scanner is now operational in Gitega. Yaga Burundi reports it is the first such device to function outside the capital in 2026.
bi.why: Patients in the interior of the country can now access diagnostic imaging without traveling to Bujumbura.

bi.headline: Burundi beats Germany in Beach Pro Tour opener
bi.body: The Burundi men's team defeated Germany in the opening match of the Volleyball World Beach Pro Tour Bujumbura Futures. The tournament runs from Aug. 19 to Aug. 23, 2026, according to Iwacu.
bi.why: The victory marks a successful start for the host nation in an international sporting competition.

bi.headline: CENI presents Gitega electoral map for 2027
bi.body: The Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI) presented the electoral mapping for Gitega province on Aug. 19. SOS Médias Burundi reports the move is part of preparations for the 2027 presidential election.
bi.why: The mapping defines the geographic boundaries and organization of polling stations for voters in the province.

bi.headline: Rusizi National Park adds biodiversity protection infrastructure
bi.body: The Rusizi National Park received new equipment and infrastructure to improve management and tourism. The handover ceremony took place Aug. 13 with representatives from the EU, UNDP, and Belgium, Iwacu reports.
bi.why: The new installations are intended to increase the protection of the reserve's biodiversity and attract more tourists.

cm.headline: Douala BRT project faces CFAF104.6 billion funding gap
cm.body: The Douala Urban Mobility Project requires an additional CFAF104.6 billion to maintain its current scope, according to project estimates as of July 17, 2026. The total cost to complete the project is now estimated at CFAF365.4 billion, up from an initial budget of CFAF260.8 billion. This shortfall represents 40.1% of the original budget.
cm.why: Without new funding or tax relief, the project may be downsized, potentially removing 66 kilometers of planned feeder roads around the pilot corridor.

cm.headline: CAMWATER targets CFAF2.35 billion in monthly collections
cm.body: The state-owned Cameroon Water Utilities Corporation set a CFAF2.35 billion revenue collection target for Douala and Yaoundé for this month. The utility expects to mobilize CFAF1.25 billion from Yaoundé and CFAF1.1 billion from Douala, according to a company disclosure on August 20.
cm.why: The push aims to increase internally generated revenue to improve the utility's overall financial performance.

cm.headline: Cameroon allocates CFAF400 million to food supply SMEs
cm.body: The government has allocated CFAF400 million to finance small and medium-sized enterprises that distribute locally produced food. The Trade Ministry announced the transfer of funds via the Cameroon Bank for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises on August 18, 2026.
cm.why: The funding targets bottlenecks in the government's import-substitution program by helping domestic producers move products to consumers.

cm.headline: Cameroon reports 45.5% BTS and 54.79% HND pass rates
cm.body: The Ministry of Higher Education published official 2026 results on August 19 showing national success rates of 45.50% for the BTS and 54.79% for the HND. These figures contradict earlier unofficial reports of a 14% success rate.
cm.why: The official release ends a period of public controversy regarding the accuracy of the national exam results.

cm.headline: Landslide at Cameroon-CAR border kills 4 Cameroonians
cm.body: Four Cameroonians died following a landslide at a gold mining site in the village of Zamboi on August 18, 2026. Local administrative authorities confirmed the deaths and stated the collapse occurred within Central African Republic territory.
cm.why: The victims' bodies have been transferred to Garoua-Boulaï on the Cameroonian side of the border.

cf.headline: Gold mine collapse kills more than 100 in Central African Republic
cf.body: The death toll from a gold mine collapse in western Central African Republic has risen above 100. Africanews reports the disaster occurred at an artisanal mine near the Cameroon border, with several people still missing.
cf.why: The incident highlights the safety risks facing thousands of informal miners operating in the region.

cf.headline: CAR presidency says courts can probe French ambassador sex scandal
cf.body: The presidency of the Central African Republic stated that national justice can take up allegations against French Ambassador Bruno Foucher. Spokesperson Albert Yalokké Mokpême issued the statement following reports from Le Canard Enchaîné regarding Foucher's conduct in Bangui.
cf.why: The statement opens the door for legal proceedings against a foreign diplomat within the country's judicial system.

cf.headline: Village of Polonda relies on one borehole for 6,000 residents
cf.body: More than 6,000 inhabitants in the village of Polonda have access to only one functioning borehole. Radio Ndeke Luka reports that a second water point has been broken for four years.
cf.why: The lack of infrastructure forces residents in four neighborhood groups to share a single water source for their daily needs.

cf.headline: GTSC accuses UNOPS of failing to rehabilitate Ndélé-Ouadda road
cf.body: The GTSC has denounced the UNOPS for failing to meet commitments to rehabilitate the Ndélé-Ouadda road and build four bridges. Spokesperson Paul Crescent Béninga stated that the World Bank has already disbursed the funds for the project.
cf.why: The failure to complete the road and bridges prevents the expected improvement of transport and connectivity between Mbrès and Ndélé.

cf.headline: Bouar hospital reports staff shortages and medicine deficits
cf.body: The Bouar health district is facing a shortage of qualified personnel and a lack of essential medicines. District chief physician Dr. Martin Zekana reported these deficiencies as factors affecting the center's operations.
cf.why: The lack of staff and supplies reduces the quality and availability of medical care for patients in the Nana-Mambéré prefecture.

km.headline: Moroni police open investigation into abduction of 6-year-old girl
km.body: A 6-year-old girl is in serious condition after being abducted and raped in Moroni. Comores Infos reports the child disappeared on Aug. 16 while traveling to her Quranic school.
km.why: The incident has prompted a formal investigation into the abduction and assault.

cg.headline: Congo sets $90 per barrel threshold for oil contracts
cg.body: The Council of Ministers approved a single threshold of $90 per barrel to adjust the contractual framework of the petroleum sector. The measures include amendments to permits Nanga II Bis, Nanga IV, Nangua V, and Marine XXIX. The government also launched a redevelopment project for the Banga Kayo permit.
cg.why: The adjustment to the technical mechanism aims to support investments and increase oil production.

cg.headline: Congo maintains cement prices for 50kg bags
cg.body: Cement prices remain unchanged at 4,900 FCFA in Brazzaville, 4,700 FCFA in Pointe-Noire, and 5,500 FCFA in Ouesso for a 50kg bag. The decision follows a meeting on Aug. 19 between the Minister of Commerce and producers Dangote, Sonocc, and Forspak. The producers had previously requested a price increase.
cg.why: The freeze prevents a price hike for construction materials despite producer demands.

cg.headline: Congo police seize six firearms from poaching suspect
cg.body: Police and eco-guards from the Lésio-Luna nature reserve seized six firearms and hundreds of munitions on Aug. 13. The items were found during a search of a home in Yono village in the Djoué-Léfini department. Authorities identified the suspect as the alleged leader of a poaching network.
cg.why: The seizure removes weaponry used for illegal hunting in the Lésio-Luna nature reserve.

cg.headline: Congo proposes National Order of Dental Surgeons
cg.body: Health Minister Jean Rosaire Ibara presented a bill to create a national professional order for dental surgeons. The project aims to modernize the structure of regulated health professions. The government stated the move is a response to patient demands for safety and competence.
cg.why: The new structure will provide oversight for the profession to improve the quality of oral healthcare for patients.

cg.headline: President Sassou-N’Guesso begins 15-day trip to Turkey
cg.body: President Denis Sassou-N’Guesso departed Brazzaville on Aug. 19 for a 15-day stay in Antalya. He is accompanied by his wife, Antoinette Sassou N’Guesso. The trip follows the president's reelection in March and recent national festivities.
cg.why: The president is taking a period of rest following a dense sequence of political and institutional activity.

ci.headline: Inspection report finds 267.8 million CFA irregularity at OCPV
ci.body: Two inspection reports identified irregularities in the management of bonuses and mutual fund payments totaling 267.8 million francs CFA. The findings concern the Office d’aide à la commercialisation des produits vivriers (OCPV) in Abidjan.
ci.why: The discovery of 'ghost bonuses' and diverted funds exposes financial mismanagement within the agency responsible for food product marketing.

ci.headline: Olympique de Marseille signs Ivorian striker Habibou Ouédraogo
ci.body: Habibou Ouédraogo joined Olympique de Marseille last week from Asec d’Abidjan. The 24-year-old attacker won the last three editions of the Ivorian Ligue 1 championship.
ci.why: The transfer moves a top-scoring player from the domestic Ivorian league to a major French club.

ci.headline: Sewé Sport president says Ivorian players cannot live on football
ci.body: Ouattara Issa, president of Sewé Sport de San Pedro, stated on August 19 that Ivorian players do not yet live fully from their sporting activity. The Ligue 2 club leader questioned the professional status of the domestic championships.
ci.why: Financial difficulties are forcing professional athletes to seek secondary employment to survive.

ci.headline: Cocody resident wins 47.4 million FCFA in PMU bets
ci.body: An entrepreneur identified as A.A. won a total of 47,442,000 FCFA. The payout followed two consecutive winning jackpots from the Loterie nationale de Côte d’Ivoire (LONACI).
ci.why: The payout represents a significant individual windfall for a resident of the Cocody district.

ci.headline: Grand-Bassam court sentences cannabis seller to 24 months prison
ci.body: The Tribunal de section de Grand-Bassam sentenced a drug trafficker to 24 months of firm imprisonment. The verdict follows a case involving the sale of cannabis.
ci.why: The ruling establishes a legal penalty for narcotics trafficking in the Grand-Bassam region.

eg.headline: Egypt secures $2 billion Chinese aluminum project in Suez Canal Zone
eg.body: Egypt has reached a deal for a $2 billion investment in a high-tech aluminum manufacturing project. Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs Hussein Issa finalized the agreement with a Chinese industrial firm.
eg.why: The project establishes an end-to-end manufacturing chain in the Suez Canal Zone to increase Egypt's global industrial footprint.

eg.headline: Egypt launches $658m phosphoric acid complex in New Valley
eg.body: Egyptian officials began construction of a $658 million industrial complex at the Abu Tartour plateau. The facility is designed to produce 250,000 tonnes of commercial phosphoric acid annually.
eg.why: The plant will produce a key fertilizer component for export via Red Sea ports to increase mining revenue.

eg.headline: Egypt signs 17 export contracts with China worth $168m
eg.body: Egyptian exporters signed 17 contracts totaling an estimated $168 million with Chinese importers. The Egyptian Commercial Service reported the deals cover sugar cane, oranges, copper, aluminum, leather, textile yarn, and flax.
eg.why: The agreements are part of a government effort to diversify the types of goods Egypt exports to the Chinese market.

eg.headline: Microbus rollover in Monufia kills 2, injures 17
eg.body: Two people died and 17 others were injured when a passenger microbus overturned on the Kafr Dawood road. The accident occurred near the village of Al-Baregat in Monufia Governorate.
eg.why: Emergency services had to deploy multiple ambulances to the scene to treat and transport the 19 casualties.

eg.headline: Egypt forecasts temperature spike of 2 degrees starting Friday
eg.body: The Egyptian Meteorological Authority announced temperatures will rise by up to two degrees beginning Friday. The agency forecasts extremely hot and humid conditions nationwide during the day.
eg.why: The heatwave will affect both inland governorates and coastal areas, increasing humidity levels across the country.

gq.headline: Diario Rombe reports 65,000 patients lack antiretrovirals
gq.body: Approximately 65,000 patients in Bata are without antiretroviral medications. Diario Rombe attributes the shortage to the Ministry of Health and Infrastructure, led by Dámaso Mitoha Ondo’o Ayekaba.
gq.why: The lack of medication increases the risk of death for patients who cannot maintain their viral suppression treatment.

gq.headline: Diario Rombe alleges secret contract for 1,000 tons of gold
gq.body: A secret contract involving 1,000 tons of gold and a $30 million bank guarantee is allegedly controlled by a relative of Constancia Mangue. Diario Rombe reports the operation functioned outside ordinary state controls.
gq.why: The existence of an unregulated gold trade circuit bypasses official state revenue and oversight mechanisms.

gq.headline: Prime Minister orders notary inspections over revenue gaps
gq.body: Prime Minister Manuel Osa has ordered inspections of notary offices after detecting gaps in tax collection. The order followed economic report presentations from the ministries of Justice, Cult, Human Rights, and Foreign Affairs.
gq.why: Increased oversight of notaries aims to recover missing government funds and close loopholes in national revenue collection.

gq.headline: Scientific Committee validates V Population and I Agricultural censuses
gq.body: The Scientific Committee has approved the strategic documents for the fifth population census and the first agricultural census. The validation took place at the Ministry of Finance, Budgets and National Planning.
gq.why: These statistical operations provide the data necessary for the government to plan infrastructure and resource allocation for farmers.

gq.headline: New Media Law proposes information sciences institute
gq.body: A proposed Media Law includes the creation of a practical institute for Information Sciences. The government detailed the plan to deputies as a mechanism to strengthen journalist training.
gq.why: The institute will establish formal standards for the professional training and certification of journalists in the country.

er.headline: Eritrea opens National Conference on Eritrean Agricultural Studies
er.body: The National Conference on Eritrean Agricultural Studies opened Aug. 20 at the National Confederation of Eritrean Workers Hall in Asmara. The event is themed “Advancing Sustainable Agri-food Systems for National Economic Growth,” according to Shabait.
er.why: The conference brings together food processors and farmers to develop systems intended to increase national economic growth.

ke.headline: IEBC sets Feb. 10 resignation deadline for public officers seeking office
ke.body: Public officers eyeing elective posts must resign by February 10, according to the IEBC. Campaigning for the elections will close on August 7, 2027.
ke.why: The deadline forces government employees to choose between their current civil service roles and running for office.

ke.headline: Helicopter crash in Kenya kills 7 including Ecuador intelligence chief
ke.body: Seven people died in a helicopter crash, including Ecuador intelligence chief Michele Sensi-Contugi and his wife Stephany Hollihan. The BBC reports the victims included five Americans.
ke.why: The deaths of the intelligence chief and his spouse prompted Ecuador to issue a security directive.

ke.headline: Swiss poll names Kalonzo as leading opposition choice with 41%
ke.body: Kalonzo leads opposition candidates with 41% support in a Swiss poll. Other results include Sifuna at 26%, Matiangi at 16%, and Gachagua at 9%.
ke.why: The figures indicate the younger electorate is becoming a central force in determining the anti-Ruto vote.

ke.headline: Sightra app uses AI to navigate visually impaired users in Nairobi
ke.body: The Sightra web app uses AI to detect cars, trees, and furniture in real time. The tool sends spoken descriptions of obstacles through an earpiece to the user.
ke.why: The technology allows people with visual impairments to identify physical obstacles while moving through the city.

ke.headline: Education CS confirms schools will open August 24
ke.body: Schools are scheduled to open for Term III on August 24. Education CS Julius Ogamba refuted social media reports that the date had been postponed.
ke.why: Parents are instructed to rely on official notices rather than social media to coordinate the return of students.

za.headline: Eastern Cape Education Department admits withholding billions from schools
za.body: The Eastern Cape Education Department admitted it unlawfully withheld billions from schools over three years. The move affected approximately 1.58 million no-fee pupils, according to Daily Maverick.
za.why: Parents already surviving on grants must now supply their own toilet paper, cleaning products and copying paper for classrooms.

za.headline: MP Fadiel Adams accuses police officials of abusing power
za.body: National Coloured Congress MP Fadiel Adams told the Madlanga Commission that KZN police commissioner Lieutenant-General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi and Crime Intelligence head Dumisani Khumalo colluded and abused power. Adams argued that Mkhwanazi should be investigated, according to the Mail & Guardian.
za.why: The testimony challenges the conduct of high-ranking police officials regarding allegations involving Crime Intelligence.

za.headline: Ndifuna Ukwazi seeks to block eviction of 160 Transnet land occupiers
za.body: Housing activists Ndifuna Ukwazi are challenging the eviction of more than 160 people from Transnet land. The evictions are scheduled for 30 September, according to GroundUp.
za.why: The court bid determines whether more than 160 residents will lose their current housing by the end of the month.

za.headline: Chidimma Adetshina challenges legal bid for deportation
za.body: Beauty queen Chidimma Adetshina is challenging efforts to have her deported from South Africa. Adetshina claims she was born in the country, according to the BBC.
za.why: The legal outcome will determine whether Adetshina is permitted to remain in South Africa or is forced to leave the country.

za.headline: Turkish exports to Africa exceed $13 billion
za.body: Turkish exports to Africa have surpassed $13 billion. A sector representative stated that growth in gateway markets including South Africa could be used to turn direct sales into local joint investments, according to Anadolu Africa.
za.why: Increased export growth may lead to the establishment of local joint investments in South Africa.

ng.headline: FAAN denies ban on e-hailing services at airports
ng.body: The Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) stated there is no ban on Uber, Bolt, or other e-hailing services at Nigerian airports. The agency said the clarification aims to improve safety and management.
ng.why: Passengers arriving at airports can continue to use mobile apps to book transport to their destinations.

ng.headline: NESG forecasts Nigeria oil output to exceed 1.7mbpd
ng.body: Crude oil production is expected to top 1.7 million barrels per day in the second half of 2026. The Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) said higher prices could improve the country's fiscal outlook.
ng.why: Increased production and pricing would provide the government with more revenue to manage national spending.

ng.headline: Gunmen kill at least 24 people in Plateau State
ng.body: Attackers killed at least 24 people in the Bin-Per community of north-central Nigeria. A lawmaker reported that the attackers also burned 38 homes.
ng.why: The destruction of 38 homes leaves families in the Bin-Per community without shelter.

ng.headline: Boat capsizes in Sokoto state killing dozens
ng.body: Dozens of people died after a boat capsized in north-western Nigeria. The incident occurred in Sokoto state, where many of the victims are feared to be children.
ng.why: The accident results in a significant loss of life, specifically affecting children in the Sokoto region.

ng.headline: Inflation and security lead voter concerns as campaigns begin
ng.body: General election campaigning began on Wednesday. Voters are seeking specific answers from candidates on how to improve citizen lives, focusing on inflation and security.
ng.why: Candidates must now provide concrete policy plans to address the rising cost of living to win voter support.

et.headline: Ethiopia joins African Circular Economy Facility implementation
et.body: Ethiopia has entered the active implementation phase of the African Circular Economy Facility. The African Development Bank manages the multi-donor trust fund.
et.why: The initiative aims to transform waste into economic value and foster green industrial development for domestic businesses.

et.headline: Egypt warns Ethiopia against building new Nile dams
et.body: Egypt has issued a warning against the construction of new Ethiopian dams on the Nile River. The warning was reported by Radio Tamazuj.
et.why: The dispute over dam construction affects the management and distribution of water resources between the two nations.

et.headline: Tigray rebels report drone strikes in Mekelle
et.body: Drone strikes hit a residential area in the Tigray regional capital of Mekelle. The Africa Report stated that civilian casualty details are currently unknown.
et.why: The air raids increase the risk of civilian casualties in residential zones of the regional capital.

gh.headline: Ghana bank advances rise 38.6% to GH¢124.3 billion
gh.body: Total bank advances reached GH¢124.3 billion in June 2026, up from GH¢89.7 billion a year earlier. Private-sector credit expanded by 41.2% during the same period. The data indicates that productive sectors are receiving relatively small shares of this credit.
gh.why: The current lending structure limits the growth of productive sectors intended to drive the 24-Hour Economy.

gh.headline: Five in six Ghana health facilities miss sanitation standards
gh.body: Approximately 83% of health facilities in Ghana fail to meet the full international standard for basic sanitation. The figures were released by WHO and UNICEF.
gh.why: The lack of clean, usable toilets in these facilities hinders the ability of patients to access basic hygiene during medical care.

gh.headline: Energy Ministry warns of power system vulnerability
gh.body: Ghana's electricity transmission system is currently vulnerable due to the use of a temporary control room. The Ministry of Energy expects a permanent facility to be completed by the end of September.
gh.why: The temporary arrangement increases the risk of system failures until the permanent facility is operational.

gh.headline: ECG schedules eight-hour outage in Ashanti Region
gh.body: The Electricity Company of Ghana announced a planned eight-hour power outage affecting several communities in the Ashanti Region. The company stated the outage is for maintenance works.
gh.why: The maintenance is intended to improve electricity service delivery for residents in the affected communities.

gh.headline: GRA resolves technical issues on Ghana.gov payment platform
gh.body: The Ghana Revenue Authority is addressing intermittent technical challenges affecting tax payments. The issues impacted the Ghana.gov payment platform.
gh.why: The resolution allows taxpayers, importers, and clearing agents to resume the payment of taxes.

cd.headline: Africa CDC mobilizes $700 million for Ebola response in DRC
cd.body: Africa CDC has mobilized $700 million to combat Ebola, with $452 million already disbursed. Director General Jean Kaseya detailed the figures during a Space live interview on Wednesday.
cd.why: The funding supports the scale of the organization's role in managing the virus outbreak.

cd.headline: DRC launches emergency Ebola measures along Congo River
cd.body: The DRC government launched an emergency system on Thursday between Kisangani and Kinshasa. According to an official statement, the measures aim to prevent the spread of the Bundibugyo virus along the country's main waterway.
cd.why: The restrictions target the primary fluvial transport route to stop the virus from moving between major cities.

cd.headline: CAVB moves 2026 Men's African Volleyball Championship to Tunis
cd.body: The African Volleyball Confederation (CAVB) officially withdrew the organization of the 2026 Men's African Nations Championship from the DRC on Thursday. The event will now be held in Tunis.
cd.why: The relocation is a result of the Ebola outbreak in the DRC.

cd.headline: AFC-M23 bans Kinshasa news in South Kivu zones
cd.body: De facto governor Patrick Busu Bwa Ngwi Shombo has prohibited the broadcast of political programs and news from Kinshasa. The ban applies to all areas under the rebellion's control in South Kivu.
cd.why: Residents in these zones are now blocked from accessing official government information and political broadcasts from the capital.

cd.headline: Provincial deputy seeks probe into illegal gold mining in Luiza
cd.body: Provincial deputy Stéphane Muanda has requested a judicial investigation into several mining companies and provincial officials. The request follows an investigative report published Saturday, Aug. 15, alleging illegal gold exploitation in the Luiza territory.
cd.why: The probe targets provincial authorities and companies to address the unauthorized extraction of mineral resources in Kasaï-Central.

tz.headline: Tanzania suspends weekly newspaper for six months
tz.body: The information ministry suspended a weekly newspaper for six months following a report alleging government divisions. The ministry cited alleged breaches of media law as the reason for the closure.
tz.why: The suspension prevents the outlet from publishing investigative reports on the Vice President and government internal conflicts.

tz.headline: Hydropower generates 63.85% of Tanzania's grid electricity
tz.body: Hydropower provided 63.85% of electricity from the national grid in 2025, according to the Tanzania Economic Survey 2025. Natural gas accounted for 31.48% of generation.
tz.why: The government is utilizing this capacity to reach a target of 3,000 kWh per capita by 2050.

tz.headline: DP World contracts EDECS to build seven cargo yards at Dar Port
tz.body: DP World has hired Egyptian firm EDECS to construct seven cargo yards at the Dar es Salaam port. The project includes physical infrastructure and digital yard management systems.
tz.why: The new yards will increase cargo storage capacity and automate the management of shipments at the port.

tz.headline: NECTA chief elected president of AEAA for 2026/2027
tz.body: Prof. Said Mohamed, Executive Secretary of the National Examinations Council of Tanzania, was elected president of the Association for Educational Assessment in Africa. He will serve the 2026/2027 term.
tz.why: The appointment gives Tanzania a leadership role in coordinating educational assessment standards across African school systems.

tz.headline: Police donate 100 items to Nyamagana District Hospital
tz.body: The Nyamagana District Police Force donated 50 bedsheets and 50 mosquito nets to patients at Nyamagana District Hospital. The handover took place in the Mwanza region.
tz.why: The donation provides immediate bedding and malaria prevention tools for patients receiving treatment at the facility.

ma.headline: Morocco enacts Law 66.23 regulating legal profession
ma.body: Law 66.23 took effect Thursday following its publication in the Official Gazette. The law was enacted by Royal Decree 1.26.75 on Aug. 18, according to the Official Gazette. A nationwide lawyers' strike against the regulation has been ongoing since June 15.
ma.why: The enactment proceeds despite an unresolved constitutional challenge and active industrial action by the country's lawyers.

ma.headline: Morocco plans 300km water canal to link Sebou and Oum Er Rbia
ma.body: Morocco is planning a water transfer project spanning approximately 300 kilometers. The system will have a transport capacity of 800 million cubic meters of water annually, according to the platform Al Ma Dialna.
ma.why: The project aims to improve the distribution of water resources between different regions to enhance national water security.

ma.headline: Moroccan mutton prices exceed 150 dirhams per kg
ma.body: Mutton prices in several Moroccan cities have risen above 150 dirhams per kilogram. Beef prices are currently ranging between 120 and 130 dirhams, according to Barlamane.
ma.why: Rising costs are reducing the purchasing power of low-income families amid criticisms that meat imports have been ineffective.

ma.headline: Algeria returns 49 migrants to Morocco
ma.body: Algerian authorities handed over 49 Moroccan migrants to Moroccan officials on Wednesday. The group included two women and two minors, according to the Moroccan Association for Aid to Migrants in Vulnerable Situations (AMSV).
ma.why: The transfer took place via the Oujda-Maghnia border crossing to return the individuals to their home country.

ma.headline: Lithuanian plant shutdown may boost Moroccan fertilizer demand
ma.body: European demand for Moroccan fertilizer could increase following the suspension of production at EuroChem's Lifosa plant in Lithuania. Argus Media reported the plant halted operations due to high raw-material costs.
ma.why: The shutdown occurs as shipping disruptions have already tightened global supplies of phosphate products.

ug.headline: Police investigate Kabalagala attack that killed 2 children
ug.body: Two children were killed and three others injured during an early-morning attack in Kabalagala. Police report that a vehicle was also burnt during the incident.
ug.why: The attack left a mother among the injured and resulted in the deaths of two children.

ug.headline: Uganda trade deficit widens to $598 million in June
ug.body: The merchandise trade deficit reached approximately $598 million in June as imports grew three times faster than exports. Nile Post reports that coffee earnings fell by more than a third.
ug.why: The decline in coffee revenue and surge in imports reduce the amount of foreign currency entering the country.

ug.headline: Court convicts 3 for murder of 6-year-old pupil
ug.body: The High court in Soroti convicted school directors Suzan Vivian Ariokot and Joseph Okedi, and police officer John Bosco Obotol, for the murder of Joan Faith Apio. The pupil was found dead with her throat slit in a school latrine on February 5, 2025.
ug.why: The ruling establishes criminal liability for the school's directors while acquitting the headteacher and matron.

ug.headline: Witness claims Besigye plotted to bomb Cafe Javas
ug.body: Investigator Andrew Wilson told the High court he used a covert camera to record meetings where Dr. Kizza Besigye discussed acquiring weapons to overthrow the government. Wilson testified that these plans included bombing Cafe Javas.
ug.why: The testimony introduces evidence of a specific plot to target a commercial establishment as part of a coup attempt.

ug.headline: Movit Africa provides tuk-tuks to Masaka traders
ug.body: Movit Africa gave tuk-tuks to three cosmetics traders in Masaka and Kyotera. The company stated the vehicles are intended to help traders move more stock.
ug.why: The new vehicles allow traders Senalim Hakim and Kalungi K to cut transport costs and reach more customers.

zw.headline: Court grants Mnangagwa daughter-in-law USD1,000 bail
zw.body: Kelsea Tadiwa Tafirenyika and co-accused Isaac Arab Jessub were granted USD1,000 bail on Thursday. Justice Pisirayi Kwenda set aside a previous magistrate's decision to keep the drug-dealing suspects in custody.
zw.why: The ruling allows the suspects to remain out of prison while awaiting trial.

zw.headline: RBZ maintains 30% export surrender requirement
zw.body: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe rejected calls to reduce the 30% export surrender threshold in its mid-term monetary policy statement released Thursday. The central bank stated the policy is necessary for price and exchange rate stability.
zw.why: Exporters must continue converting nearly one-third of their foreign currency earnings into local currency.

zw.headline: RBZ injects ZiG600 million into circulation
zw.body: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe added approximately ZiG600 million to the economy during the first half of 2026. The move aims to increase the use of the local currency.
zw.why: The injection is intended to ease cash-related challenges for businesses and consumers.

zw.headline: Zimbabwe launches tracking system to stop drug theft
zw.body: The government introduced a medicine tracking system to prevent the theft of drugs from public hospitals. Deputy Health Minister Sleiman Kwidini said employees have been stealing medication for resale in private pharmacies.
zw.why: The system aims to ensure medications intended for public patients reach their destination rather than being diverted to the private market.

zw.headline: Contractors seek private consultants to recover ZiG250 billion
zw.body: Contractors are pursuing private consultants to recover outstanding state payments estimated by the Auditor-General at ZiG250 billion. The move follows a government backlash against the use of such consultants.
zw.why: Firms are attempting to resolve deepening cash-flow problems caused by the unpaid state debts.

cv.headline: Cape Verde opens 55,719 new payment accounts in 2025
cv.body: A total of 55,719 new payment accounts were opened in 2025, according to a recent report. The system recorded 439,973 resident individual accounts by the end of the year, meaning 85.6% of the resident population now holds at least one bank account.
cv.why: The increase in account holders coincides with a reduction in physical infrastructure, as the number of bank branches fell from 129 to 127 due to the use of banking agents.

cv.headline: Cape Verde maintains US fiscal transparency status
cv.body: Cape Verde is among 73 nations that fully meet minimum budget integrity and public account management requirements. The status was confirmed in the latest US Department of State Fiscal Transparency Report.
cv.why: The designation is intended to strengthen the country's reputation with multilateral creditors, foreign investors, and development partners.

cv.headline: Cape Verde government meets mayors to align budget priorities
cv.body: Prime Minister Francisco Carvalho held meetings with mayors from Santiago island to coordinate local priorities with the State Budget. Carvalho stated the government is conducting a round of direct dialogues with all municipalities.
cv.why: The meetings aim to ensure that local territorial needs are integrated into the national spending plan under a logic of equality.

cv.headline: São Vicente reports zero dengue cases amid monthly mosquito studies
cv.body: Health authorities in São Vicente have recorded no cases of dengue despite the presence of vectors. According to official Celso Martins, the Health Delegation is conducting monthly entomological studies and monitoring ports and airports.
cv.why: The surveillance system allows the island to identify malaria cases as primarily imported from endemic zones rather than locally transmitted.

cv.headline: Health unions seek urgent salary updates for technicians
cv.body: Unions met with the Minister of Health to demand the implementation of Career, Function, and Remuneration Plans (PCFR). Representative Luís Lima stated the ministry has acknowledged the professional claims and the existing PCFR processes.
cv.why: The requested updates would change the pay scales and career progression for auxiliary health technicians.

td.headline: Community clashes kill 6 in Batha region
td.body: Six people, including one woman, died and 10 others were injured during clashes in Alkhaba on Aug. 20. Tchadinfos reports the violence began following a dispute over the exploitation of a field.
td.why: The conflict disrupts local agricultural activity for farmers in the Oum-Hadjer area.

td.headline: Chad and Libya plan N'Djamena-Tripoli flight route
td.body: The Chadian foreign minister and Libyan authorities agreed in Tripoli to reopen the N'Djamena-Tripoli air line. The two nations also plan to establish a dry port in Misrata.
td.why: The new transport corridors will increase the movement of goods and passengers between the two capitals.

td.headline: Ndjamena faces power outages after Farcha plant fire
td.body: Recurring power outages have hit several neighborhoods in Ndjamena following a fire at the Farcha 1 thermal power plant in late July. RFI Afrique reports authorities are installing mobile plants and recruiting independent producers to stabilize the grid.
td.why: The energy shortage disrupts business operations and daily household activities for residents in the capital.

td.headline: Doba launches sanitation drive to prevent cholera
td.body: The city of Doba began a large-scale operation to clear gutters and remove waste on Aug. 20. Mayor Misdongarti Nodjinan initiated the cleanup in the Bedogo, Tinmbi, and Gaki neighborhoods.
td.why: The cleanup aims to reduce stagnant water and waste to prevent a cholera outbreak among city residents.

td.headline: Gold mine collapse in CAR kills at least 49
td.body: At least 49 people died after a gold mine collapsed in Zamboï on the border between Cameroon and the Central African Republic. Official reports state the victims include Chadians, Cameroonians, and Central Africans.
td.why: The disaster affects mining families and laborers operating across the border region.

dj.headline: Djibouti economy grew 6.7% in 2025
dj.body: Djibouti's economy grew 6.7% in 2025, down from 6.8% in 2024. The African Development Bank attributed the growth to telecommunications, energy, trade, construction, and port and logistics activities.
dj.why: The growth in port and logistics activities increases the volume of goods moving through the country's primary infrastructure.

sz.headline: Eswatini to pave 250km of roads for E1.6 billion
sz.body: Approximately 250 kilometers of untarred roads across four regions will be paved using Probase tarring at a cost of E1.6 billion. The project was discussed during a visit by Probase and Exim Bank officials to the King, according to the King's Office. This infrastructure investment improves transport connectivity for residents and businesses across the country's four regions.
sz.why: The paving of untarred roads reduces travel time and vehicle wear for commuters and commercial transporters in the four regions.

sz.headline: MPs pass motion to establish health fund levies
sz.body: Members of Parliament have passed a motion to create a fund for collecting levies to fight serious diseases. The motion was moved by MP Marwick Khumalo and seconded by MP Sandile Nxumalo. The fund will provide a dedicated financial stream to procure treatments and resources for patients with critical illnesses.
sz.why: The establishment of these levies creates a new funding source specifically for the treatment of serious diseases.

sz.headline: King gives US$1,000 to Eswatini students in Malaysia
sz.body: Eswatini students studying in Malaysia each received a contribution of US$1,000, or approximately E16,000. Minister for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Pholile Shakantu announced the gift during a courtesy call. The funds provide direct financial support for the living and academic expenses of students abroad.
sz.why: The payment provides immediate liquidity to students in Malaysia to cover their welfare and educational costs.

sz.headline: Comrades Marathon offers E8.9m purse for Eswatini athletes
sz.body: A prize purse of E8.9 million is available for elite Eswatini athletes in the 100th Comrades Marathon. The centenary edition of the ultramarathon is scheduled for June 13, 2027, according to an announcement at Kings Park Rugby Stadium. The prize money provides a financial incentive for elite runners to enter the centenary event.
sz.why: The E8.9 million purse allows elite athletes to pursue professional training and competition in the centenary ultramarathon.

sz.headline: SBS Bank schedules first AGM as commercial bank
sz.body: SBS Bank Eswatini will hold its first annual general meeting on September 4, 2026, at the Royal Villas Hotel. The meeting follows the institution's transition from the Swaziland Building Society into a commercial bank, according to the Times of Eswatini. This transition allows the bank to offer a broader range of commercial banking services to its customers.
sz.why: The conversion to a commercial bank enables the institution to provide expanded financial products beyond those of a building society.

ga.headline: Agasa immobilizes 10 bread transport vehicles in Estuaire
ga.body: The Gabonese Food Safety Agency (Agasa) has immobilized 10 vehicles in the Estuaire region since Aug. 14. The agency is conducting a national compliance campaign for vehicles transporting bread and bakery products.
ga.why: Non-compliant transporters face vehicle seizure and operational halts to meet food safety standards.

ga.headline: Gabon cancels study scholarships to France from September
ga.body: Study scholarships for students heading to France will be suppressed starting in September 2026. Lawyer Charlène Ongotha has questioned the legal basis and authority behind the measure.
ga.why: Gabonese students lose state funding for French degrees and must seek legal or alternative financial recourse.

ga.headline: ANBG signs pact to expand vocational training access
ga.body: The National Scholarship Agency of Gabon (ANBG) and the National Agency for Professional Training and Education (ANFEP) signed a collaboration agreement on Aug. 19. The deal aims to increase access for scholarship students to vocational training.
ga.why: Bursary students can now pivot from traditional academic paths to professional certifications within Gabon.

ga.headline: Mougoutsi fish station lacks budget for feed
ga.body: The Mougoutsi fish station in Tchibanga is facing a shortage of fish feed. Minister of the Sea, Fisheries and Blue Economy Aimé Martial Massamba identified the budget gap during a recent mission to Nyanga.
ga.why: The lack of feed prevents the public infrastructure from utilizing its production potential to supply fish.

ga.headline: VAALCO names Hermélia Hayes Mbadinga as Gabon Country Manager
ga.body: VAALCO has appointed Hermélia Hayes Mbadinga as General Administrator and Country Manager of VAALCO Gabon S.A. The appointment was announced by group CEO George Maxwell.
ga.why: The leadership change establishes a new executive head for the company's petroleum operations in Gabon.

gm.headline: Coalition 2026 signs alliance of eight parties
gm.body: Eight political parties and movements, including the People's Right Party and FORWARD Gambia, are signing a political alliance today. The agreement will be signed at Pencha Mi Hall, according to a coalition statement.
gm.why: The alliance aims to consolidate support ahead of the presidential election on December 5.

gm.headline: PPA quits merger with Gambia For All
gm.body: The Patriotic Progressive Alliance (PPA) has dissolved its merger with Gambia For All. A statement from the PPA said the movement will now join the Unite/NUP alliance.
gm.why: The shift changes the composition of political blocs competing in the 2026 election.

gm.headline: Gambia to play Somalia at Independence Stadium
gm.body: The national team's first Afcon 2027 qualifier against Somalia will be played at the Independence Stadium next month. Coach Jonathon McKinstry announced the venue in a message to players.
gm.why: This marks the first time since McKinstry took over in May 2024 that the team will play a home match.

gm.headline: Minister cites mathematics teacher shortage
gm.body: A shortage of mathematics teachers remains a major challenge for schools, according to Dr. Drammeh. Speaking to QTV on August 18, she noted that some schools currently have no math teachers.
gm.why: The shortage is compounded by low tertiary enrollment and student fear of the subject, impacting academic performance.

gm.headline: Ismaila Kone pleads not guilty to murder
gm.body: Ismaila Kone pleaded not guilty to one count of murder before Principal Magistrate M. Krubally. Prosecutors allege Kone caused the death of Isatou Elizabeth Mendy on August 17 at Lovell Square Street in Banjul.
gm.why: The legal proceedings will determine if Kone is held accountable under Section 155 of the Criminal Offences Act 2025.

gn.headline: Guinea creates 2 new administrative regions
gn.body: President Mamadi Doumbouya established Beyla and Siguiri as new administrative regions on Thursday, Aug. 20. The move was announced via an official act restructuring the country's territorial division. These areas previously served as prefectures.
gn.why: The restructuring changes the administrative hierarchy for local officials and residents in Beyla and Siguiri.

gn.headline: President Doumbouya creates 11 new prefectures
gn.body: President Mamadi Doumbouya created 11 new prefectures on Thursday, Aug. 20. A regulatory act from the Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralization will define their organization and operation.
gn.why: The decree grants these 11 localities the status of full-exercise administrative entities.

gn.headline: Guinea's High Council of the Judiciary revokes Algassimou Diallo
gn.body: The High Council of the Judiciary permanently revoked Algassimou Diallo from the judiciary on Aug. 20. Diallo, a former general advocate at the Supreme Court, had been suspended on Aug. 18 for failing to meet statutory obligations.
gn.why: The decision ends the legal career of a magistrate known for his role in the trial regarding the events of Sept. 28, 2009.

gn.headline: Ignace Deen hospital gives patients 72 hours to vacate
gn.body: Patients at the Ignace Deen hospital in Kaloum were ordered on Thursday to leave the facility within 72 hours. The order is part of a project to reconstruct and modernize the hospital.
gn.why: Patients with medical probes and other critical needs are being forced to find alternative care during the reconstruction.

gn.headline: Guinea bids to host 2032 and 2036 Africa Cup of Nations
gn.body: Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah signed the official bid dossiers for Guinea to host the 2032 and 2036 editions of the Africa Cup of Nations. The signature followed a working meeting dedicated to the candidacy.
gn.why: The bid seeks to bring the continental football tournament to Guinea for the first time in those specific years.

gw.headline: CNE bars parties from Aug. 30 referendum campaign
gw.body: Political parties are excluded from participating in the campaign for the Aug. 30 referendum. National Election Commission President Carmem Isaura Tavares Batista Lobo cited the Referendum Law as the basis for the restriction.
gw.why: The ruling prevents organized political parties from officially mobilizing voters or funding campaigns for the upcoming vote.

gw.headline: PAIGC calls for boycott of constitutional referendum
gw.body: The Permanent Commission of the African Party for the Independence of Guinea and Cape Verde (PAIGC) rejected the upcoming constitutional referendum. The party has called for a boycott of the vote.
gw.why: The boycott effort seeks to undermine the legitimacy of the constitutional changes by reducing voter turnout.

gw.headline: MRPT labels constitutional referendum a 'sham'
gw.body: The Revolutionary Movement of the Soil (MRPT) opposed the constitutional referendum scheduled for Aug. 30. The group described the process as a 'simulacrum' and urged citizens to boycott the vote.
gw.why: The call for a boycott aims to delegitimize the legal process used to alter the country's constitution.

gw.headline: Guiné Telecom and INSS sign worker social security pact
gw.body: Guiné Telecom and the National Institute of Social Security (INSS) signed an agreement on Aug. 20. The deal aims to regularize the social security status of workers.
gw.why: The agreement allows employees of the telecommunications firm to access social security benefits and legal protections.

gw.headline: Mini-Football Association prioritizes talent scouting
gw.body: The Guinean Mini-Football Association (AMF-GB) has set staff training and talent scouting as its primary goals. President Califa Soares Cassamá announced the priorities today.
gw.why: The focus on scouting and training aims to increase the number of qualified coaches and competitive players in the sport.

lr.headline: Liberia collects US$904.7 million in domestic revenue
lr.body: The Liberia Revenue Authority reported US$904.7 million in domestic revenue collection as of August 18. The figure brings the government close to a US$1 billion mark.
lr.why: Increased domestic resource mobilization allows the government to fund public projects without relying solely on external borrowing.

lr.headline: Liberia implicates former VP Jewel Howard-Taylor in US$317M drug case
lr.body: Former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor is implicated in a cocaine seizure valued at US$317 million. The investigation involves high-ranking officials, according to reports.
lr.why: The probe targets organized drug trafficking and the laundering of proceeds within the country's political leadership.

lr.headline: Prison Fellowship Liberia provides tuition for 525 children
lr.body: The Promise Path initiative is providing tuition fees and school supplies for 525 children of incarcerated parents. The program also introduces livelihood opportunities.
lr.why: The support ensures that children of prisoners can remain in school despite the loss of parental income.

lr.headline: AMEU and University of Sierra Leone renew academic partnership
lr.body: The African Methodist Episcopal University and the Institute of Public Administration and Management at the University of Sierra Leone reaffirmed their partnership on Tuesday. The agreement focuses on joint research and faculty and student exchanges.
lr.why: The renewal enables students and faculty to access postgraduate opportunities and knowledge transfer across the two regional institutions.

lr.headline: Ganta Business Association warns of unofficial commerce inspectors
lr.body: Members of the Ganta Business Association have raised concerns over unemployed commerce agents acting as unofficial inspectors in Nimba County. The group claims the practice undermines regulatory functions.
lr.why: The presence of unofficial inspectors increases corruption risks for local businesses and threatens public safety.

ly.headline: Spanish exports to Libya rise 114.6%
ly.body: Spanish exports to Libya increased by 114.6% and Libyan imports to Spain rose 66.8% during the first six months of the year. The Spanish Embassy in Libya provided the data.
ly.why: The growth indicates a significant increase in the volume of goods moving between the two nations' markets.

ly.headline: Libya distributes 300 solar refrigerators for medical supplies
ly.body: The National Centre for Disease Control distributed more than 300 solar-powered refrigerators. The move aims to mitigate the impact of extensive power cuts and blackouts.
ly.why: The equipment prevents medical supplies from perishing during summer electricity failures.

ly.headline: Libya and Chad resume direct flights
ly.body: Direct flights between Libya and Chad are scheduled to resume tomorrow. The arrangement follows a meeting between Prime Minister Abdel Hamid Aldabaiba and the Chadian Foreign Minister.
ly.why: The resumption of flights restores direct air travel and movement between the two countries.

ly.headline: Benghazi Court terminates Al-Kharafi land lease
ly.body: The North Benghazi Court terminated a land lease agreement with the Kuwaiti company Al-Kharafi. The ruling also nullifies an international arbitration award.
ly.why: The decision removes the Kuwaiti company's legal right to the leased land and the associated financial award.

ly.headline: Libya detains 9 people for citizenship forgery
ly.body: The Public Prosecutor ordered the detention of a civil registry employee and eight beneficiaries in Al-Khums. The group is accused of forging documents to grant citizenship rights to foreigners.
ly.why: The arrests target the illegal acquisition of citizenship rights through the manipulation of official civil status data.

mg.headline: SADC backs Madagascar's Refondation with governance conditions
mg.body: The Southern African Development Community (SADC) encouraged Madagascar to return to constitutional normality following its 46th Summit in Durban. The organization's support is contingent on recommendations regarding human rights, accountability, and citizen participation.
mg.why: The conditions require the government to implement democratic reforms and inclusive governance to maintain regional diplomatic support.

mg.headline: President Randrianirina pushes political dialogue for elections
mg.body: President Michaël Randrianirina stated that ongoing political consultations are intended to accelerate the holding of elections. The head of state made the comments upon returning from the SADC summit in Durban.
mg.why: The dialogue is designed to provide technical and political support to the CENI in preparing for upcoming electoral deadlines.

mg.headline: Antananarivo residents face renewed water and power outages
mg.body: Water pressure drops and power cuts have returned to several districts of the capital over the last few days. Utility provider JIRAMA announced that these disruptions are expected to continue into next week.
mg.why: The instability of basic utilities disrupts daily household activities and business operations for residents in the capital.

mg.headline: Mpox vaccinations begin at Polyteknika Vontovorona
mg.body: Vaccinations against Mpox are currently being administered at the Polyteknika Vontovorona campus. Health officials are conducting awareness campaigns to encourage students to protect themselves from the virus.
mg.why: The targeted campaign aims to prevent an outbreak of the virus among the student population.

mg.headline: Madagascar expands express road by 30 km
mg.body: A new express road project will extend the existing infrastructure by 30 kilometers. The project is categorized as an infrastructure expansion.
mg.why: The extension of the high-speed route increases the capacity for the movement of goods and people across the region.

mw.headline: Malawi court to rule on Sylvester Namiwa bail
mw.body: Judge Mzonde Mvula will deliver a ruling on the bail application for jailed rights activist Sylvester Namiwa at 10 a.m. today. The decision follows weeks of proceedings in a treason case.
mw.why: The ruling determines whether the activist will remain in detention or be released pending his trial.

mw.headline: Escom warns of blackouts as generation shortfall hits 83MW
mw.body: The national grid is facing a generation shortfall of 42MW, which increases to 83MW during evening peak hours. The Electricity Supply Corporation of Malawi reported that available capacity is currently 347MW.
mw.why: The deficit at the Nkula plant will lead to more frequent power outages for residential and business consumers.

mw.headline: Malawi High Court releases K383m to Nema Farm Seeds
mw.body: The High Court's Commercial Division lifted a preservation order on more than K383 million belonging to a local businessperson. The court ruled there were no grounds to suspect the funds were linked to criminal activity.
mw.why: The ruling allows Nema Farm Seeds to regain access to capital previously frozen by the Financial Intelligence Authority.

mw.headline: Malawi to open gold buying centres in September
mw.body: The government plans to establish legal gold markets in major mining areas starting in September. MAMICO CEO Leonard Kalindekafe estimated that more than US$700 million worth of gold leaves the country annually via smuggling.
mw.why: The new centers aim to reduce illegal smuggling and increase government revenue from the mining sector.

mw.headline: President Mutharika gives Scorchers players K5m each
mw.body: President Peter Mutharika awarded K5 million to each player of the Scorchers national team. The reward follows the team's campaign at the Wafcon in Rabat, Morocco.
mw.why: The payment serves as a financial incentive for the athletes after they reached the final and qualified for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

ml.headline: San residents donate 1 million CFA to military
ml.body: Residents of San delivered more than 1 million CFA to camp officials on Aug. 19. The donation was made in the presence of regional governor Colonel-Major Ousmane Sangaré.
ml.why: The funds are intended to support defense and security forces following an attack on the camp.

ml.headline: HRW accuses Africa Corps of killing 9 civilians
ml.body: Russian Africa Corps paramilitaries killed nine civilians, including four minors, on July 10 in Bombori. Human Rights Watch reported the deaths, along with lootings and house fires, in a report published Aug. 20.
ml.why: The operation took place in the Mopti region of central Mali alongside Malian soldiers.

ml.headline: Mali-Mètre poll shows 14.2 point drop in optimism
ml.body: Perceptions that the general situation in Mali has improved over the last 12 months fell by 14.2 points in one year. The Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung (FES) Mali released the 17th edition of its political opinion survey on Aug. 19.
ml.why: Citizens maintain high expectations for improvements in employment, security, and essential services.

ml.headline: Transport costs double in Macina and Ténenkou
ml.body: The cost of travel from Ségou to Macina rose to 4,000 CFA from 2,000 CFA before the crisis. Trips between Ténenkou and Macina now cost up to 7,500 CFA, compared to 2,000 CFA two years ago.
ml.why: Increased travel expenses are making movement more expensive for local residents.

ml.headline: Chiaka Magassa sworn in as Ségou governor
ml.body: Chiaka Magassa took the oath of office on Aug. 19 at the Tribunal de grande instance. Magassa, a former technical advisor at the Ministry of Territorial Administration, replaces Police Brigadier General Soulaïmane Traoré.
ml.why: The appointment establishes new regional leadership for the city of Ségou.

mr.headline: Mauritania to recruit 1,132 education agents
mr.body: The Ministry of Education and Reform of the Educational System announced a recruitment competition for 1,132 agents starting Sept. 3. The intake includes 891 teachers and 241 middle school professors.
mr.why: The recruitment opens employment opportunities for Mauritanians aged 20 and older.

mr.headline: Mauritanian coast guard rescues 315 migrants
mr.body: Coast guard officials rescued 315 people from a makeshift boat near Nouadhibou on Wednesday. The vessel was traveling from Gambia and carried migrants from Senegal and Gambia.
mr.why: The operation prevents the loss of life for migrants attempting clandestine immigration by sea.

mr.headline: Mauritania offers 160 higher education options for 2026 graduates
mr.body: The Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research announced orientation results for the first 2026 baccalaureate session. The options include 131 programs within the country and 29 abroad.
mr.why: The distribution determines which students will study domestically versus those who will move abroad for their degrees.

mr.headline: Teacher unions announce sit-in at education ministry
mr.body: The 'Hadiroun' union group, representing 12 education organizations, will begin a sit-in at the Ministry of Education on Aug. 31. The group is protesting its exclusion.
mr.why: The protest signals labor unrest among educators that could disrupt administrative operations at the ministry.

mr.headline: Nouakchott residents protest mobile tower construction
mr.body: Residents in several Nouakchott neighborhoods are opposing the installation of telecommunications pylons on public squares. A company representative told local authorities they possess documents authorizing the installations.
mr.why: The dispute pits the expansion of mobile network infrastructure against the preservation of public community spaces.

mu.headline: Supreme Court annuls release of inspector in Rs 75.9M drug case
mu.body: The Supreme Court overturned the release of inspector Vicky Luckmun involving the importation of Rs 75.9 million in synthetic drugs. The ruling was reported by Defi Media.
mu.why: The decision reinstates legal proceedings against the officer involved in the high-value narcotics seizure.

mu.headline: Mauritius agricultural price index drops 2.6% in Q2
mu.body: The Producer Price Index-Agriculture fell 2.6% between the first and second quarters of 2026, moving from 96.2 in March to 94.0 in June. Statistics Mauritius published the data on August 19.
mu.why: The decline was driven by a 5.8% drop in crop product indices, affecting the revenue of farmers producing vegetable goods.

mu.headline: Mauritius water production falls 17.8% as reservoirs deplete
mu.body: Overall water production decreased by 17.8% compared to the previous year, according to Central Water Authority figures reported in late July. Ion News noted that the Mare aux Vacoas reservoir has been particularly affected by rainfall deficits.
mu.why: Lower reservoir levels threaten the consistent supply of potable water to residents and businesses.

mu.headline: Mauritian call centers pivot after France bans phone solicitation
mu.body: Mauritian call centers are adapting their operations following a ban on telephone solicitation in France. The shift was reported by Defi Media.
mu.why: The regulatory change in France forces these centers to find new revenue streams or change their outreach methods to avoid losing contracts.

mu.headline: Ministry distributes safety gear to fishers at 2 locations
mu.body: The ministry of Agro-industry provided first aid kits, coolers, and distress beacons to fishers in Bambous-Virieux and Mahébourg on August 19. Minister Arvin Boolell stated the program will expand to all 14 fishing posts nationwide.
mu.why: The equipment allows fishers to venture further beyond the lagoon while maintaining safety and preserving catches.

mz.headline: ExxonMobil awards $1.1 billion in Rovuma LNG equipment contracts
mz.body: ExxonMobil Mozambique awarded approximately $1.1 billion in pre-investment contracts for long-term critical equipment. The contracts support Phase 1 of the Rovuma LNG project in Cabo Delgado province, according to the company.
mz.why: The investment accelerates the development of the gas field, moving the project closer to operational production.

mz.headline: BCI first-half profit falls to 3.3 billion meticais
mz.body: Profit for Banco Comercial e de Investimentos fell to 3.3 billion meticais from 3.7 billion meticais in the same period of 2025. The bank cited a spike in reserves due to high credit risk from non-performing loans, according to O Pais.
mz.why: Increased reserves for bad loans reduce the bank's available capital for lending and shareholder returns.

mz.headline: Mozambique collects $43.83 million from Rovuma gas in first half
mz.body: The state collected $43.83 million from the production and export of liquefied natural gas from the Rovuma basin between January and June 2026. Total collections rose to $296.65 million, according to the Economic and Social Plan and State Budget balance.
mz.why: These revenues provide the government with foreign currency to fund public spending and infrastructure.

mz.headline: Over 9,000 Mozambicans find work abroad since January
mz.body: More than 9,000 citizens were placed in the mining and farming sectors in South Africa since the start of the year. National Directorate of Migratory Labor Director Alice Brito said recruitment is also underway in Portugal and the UAE.
mz.why: The placement of workers increases remittance flows back into the Mozambican economy.

mz.headline: Police commander and two foreigners detained for illegal mining
mz.body: The police commander of Chinde district, a Portuguese citizen, and a Chinese citizen were detained Monday. The three are suspected of the illegal exploitation of tantalite, according to the Customs Court of Sofala and the Mozambican Police.
mz.why: The arrests target the illicit extraction of minerals that bypasses state taxation and regulation.

na.headline: Namibia non-bank sector assets reach N$552.8 billion
na.body: Namibia's non-bank financial sector assets have grown to more than N$552.8 billion. Imanuel Hawanga, general manager of capital markets at NAMFISA, also estimated the broader capital market ecosystem at N$338.2 billion.
na.why: The growth increases the capacity of non-bank institutions to mobilize savings and finance economic activity.

na.headline: Khomas100 attracts 400 cyclists from 14 countries
na.body: More than 400 cyclists from 14 countries have confirmed participation for the Khomas100 gravel cycling event on August 22. The event will host the CAC African Continental Gravel Championships.
na.why: The record international field increases the global profile of Namibian gravel cycling.

na.headline: Walvis Bay gives car wash operators 14 days to vacate
na.body: The Walvis Bay municipality has given car wash operators 14 days to leave road reserves along Sam Nujoma Avenue and Independence Road. The municipality stated the businesses lacked required permits and approvals.
na.why: Operators face the loss of their businesses and the resulting loss of livelihoods for their workers.

na.headline: Namibian Cabinet approves oil and gas local content policy
na.body: Cabinet has approved the National Upstream Petroleum Local Content Policy. Kornelia Shilunga, head of the Upstream Petroleum Unit, announced the approval on Wednesday.
na.why: The policy creates a framework to increase the participation of Namibian entities in the emerging oil and gas industry.

na.headline: Namibia introduces new business employment permit
na.body: The ministry of home affairs, immigration, safety and security has introduced the Employment Permit to Conduct Business. The permit was established through an amendment to Regulation 17 of the Immigration Control Act, 1993.
na.why: The new permit simplifies the process for foreign investors and businesspersons to establish operations in the country.

ne.headline: Niger signs $1.9 billion refinery deal with Zimar
ne.body: Niger has contracted the Canadian group Zimar to build a refinery in Dosso for $1.9 billion. The deal has caused doubt among government officials due to the group's lack of an international track record.
ne.why: The project aims to increase domestic fuel processing capacity but faces internal government skepticism over the contractor's credibility.

ne.headline: Niamey court records 420 infractions
ne.body: The Niamey High Court recorded 420 total infractions during a review on Aug. 14. The Public Prosecutor stated that these cases were largely terrorist in nature.
ne.why: The high volume of terrorism-related charges increases the judicial workload for the Niamey prosecutor's office.

ne.headline: AES holds sovereignty conference in Niamey
ne.body: The National Commission of the Confederation of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) held a conference on Aug. 19. The event took place at the Palais des Congrès for the population of Niamey.
ne.why: The conference seeks to educate Niamey residents on the confederation's goals regarding national sovereignty.

ne.headline: Agadez begins entrance exams for Excellence High Schools
ne.body: The Governor's office of Agadez launched written entrance exams for the Lycées d'Excellence on Aug. 20. The tests were administered at the CES Maï Manga Oumara.
ne.why: The exams determine which students in the Agadez region will gain admission to specialized high-performance schools.

rw.headline: AfDB plans $400 million for Rwanda agriculture
rw.body: The African Development Bank plans to invest more than $400 million into Rwanda's agriculture sector over the next three years. The bank intends to shift some of its funding priorities to support the sector.
rw.why: The funding will provide capital for farmers to transition their production methods over the three-year period.

rw.headline: Rwanda low birth weight rate rises to 8.8%
