rw.body: The proportion of babies born weighing less than 2.5 kilograms reached 8.8% in 2025. The National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda reported the figure in the Rwanda Demographic and Health Survey (RDHS7).
rw.why: The increase in low birth weight babies affects neonatal health outcomes for infants born below the 2.5 kilogram threshold.

rw.headline: Rwanda targets 100,000 hectares for conservation farming
rw.body: The government has set a target to cultivate more than 100,000 hectares using conservation agriculture. The Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board is seeking large-scale machinery to support this goal for the 2027A season.
rw.why: The acquisition of machinery allows the government to expand climate-smart farming across larger areas of land.

rw.headline: Rwanda and South Korea sign police cooperation pact
rw.body: Rwanda and South Korea have signed an agreement to strengthen cooperation between their police forces. The pact includes intelligence sharing and the fight against transnational crime.
rw.why: The agreement enables the two countries to share intelligence to combat cross-border crime and protect citizens abroad.

rw.headline: WFP delivers 5,000 metric tonnes of rice to three nations
rw.body: The United Nations World Food Programme and DP World delivered 5,000 metric tonnes of rice to support Rwanda, the DRC, and Burundi. The shipment arrived at the Port of Dar es Salaam in Tanzania from India.
rw.why: The rice shipment provides immediate food relief to communities in Rwanda facing acute food insecurity.

st.headline: Sao Tome installs 8 water systems to cut shortages
st.body: The government is installing 8 modular water collection and distribution systems across the country. In Agostinho Neto, the systems will capture 100 cubic meters of treated water per hour, according to reports.
st.why: The new infrastructure aims to reduce water scarcity for residents in affected localities.

st.headline: Constitutional Court delays party list for Sept. 27 polls
st.body: The Constitutional Court of Sao Tome and Principe has not yet validated the list of political parties admitted to the Sept. 27 legislative elections. Under Article 41 of the electoral law, judges have 11 working days to decide on the admission of candidacies.
st.why: The delay leaves the final field of competing parties unconfirmed as the election date approaches.

st.headline: 6 de Setembro leads national division with 30 points
st.body: The 15th round of the 1st division National Championship begins Friday, Aug. 21, with Agrosport de Monte Café facing Inter do Bombom. League leader 6 de Setembro holds 30 points heading into its Saturday match, according to STP Press.
st.why: The upcoming matches determine if 6 de Setembro can maintain its lead over challengers like Caixão Grande and V.Riboque.

st.headline: Director Jessica Lima joins FilmLab Mozambique
st.body: Sao Tomean director Jessica Adelaide Lombá da Silva e Lima has been selected for the first edition of FilmLab Mozambique. The intensive project development laboratory begins Aug. 24 in Maputo.
st.why: The program aims to strengthen cinematic ties and professional development for the director in Mozambique.

st.headline: Government organizes gastronomy fair for Aug. 23
st.body: The Ministry of Environment, Youth and Sustainable Tourism will hold the 'Grande Feira Gastronómica' this Sunday, Aug. 23. The event begins at 12:00 at Praça Yon Gato in the capital.
st.why: The fair provides a platform for local food vendors and tourism promotion in the capital.

sn.headline: Senegal National Assembly creates probe into tax exemptions
sn.body: The National Assembly adopted a resolution Thursday to create a parliamentary commission of inquiry into the management of tax exemptions and debt write-offs. The probe targets several hundred billion FCFA in fiscal waivers. The resolution was proposed by the PASTEF party.
sn.why: The investigation seeks to uncover the scale of lost state revenue from corporate and individual tax breaks.

sn.headline: Senegal expresses concern over U.S. sanctions on ICC official
sn.body: The Senegalese government expressed deep concern Thursday following U.S. sanctions announced Aug. 18 against International Criminal Court officials. The sanctions target Abdoulaye Seye, a member of the ICC Prosecutor's Office and a Senegalese candidate for a judge position.
sn.why: The measures affect a Senegalese national's candidacy and standing within the international judicial system.

sn.headline: Senegal opposition urges President Faye to set local election date
sn.body: Opposition parties are calling on President Bassirou Diomaye Faye to establish a date for local elections. The request follows tensions between the president and former ally Ousmane Sonko.
sn.why: The timing of the vote will determine when political challengers can contest local administrative control.

sn.headline: Sonko threatens inquiry into Dakar airport land plots
sn.body: National Assembly President Ousmane Sonko has requested clarifications from the Minister of Justice regarding irregular land subdivisions around Dakar airport. Sonko has threatened to launch a parliamentary commission of inquiry into the sites.
sn.why: The probe targets illegal land allocations that affect property ownership and urban planning near the capital's airport.

sn.headline: Linguère police arrest 4 for drug trafficking
sn.body: The Linguère urban police station arrested four individuals for criminal association, possession, trafficking, and use of drugs. The arrests were carried out by local authorities.
sn.why: The operation removes four suspected traffickers and their drug supply from the Linguère community.

sc.headline: Postal Service begins Shein parcel deliveries
sc.body: The Postal Service has taken over the delivery of Shein parcels. Chief Executive for the Postal Sector Neddy Padayachy said the service began approximately one month ago.
sc.why: Customers ordering from the online retailer now receive their goods via the national postal network.

sl.headline: Sungrow commissions first national-scale power project in Sierra Leone
sl.body: Sungrow has commissioned the RESPITE Solar-plus-Storage Project, the first national-scale power generation project connected to the grid in nearly a decade. The company is a provider of PV inverters and energy storage systems.
sl.why: The project increases the country's grid capacity through the introduction of solar and storage technology.

sl.headline: Njala University opens new agric lab with 1 million euro EU grant
sl.body: Njala University's Department of Aquaculture and Fisheries Management opened a new living lab using enclosed agricultural technology. Coordinator Dr. Olufemi Julius Olapade said the project received 1 million euros in funding from the European Union.
sl.why: The facility introduces circular technologies to create sustainable food systems for cities and regions in Africa.

sl.headline: Sierra Leone launches Gender Accountability Framework
sl.body: The Ministry of Gender and Children's Affairs and UN Women launched the Gender Accountability Framework and the 2025 Annual Report on the Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment Act 2022. The report tracks the implementation of the 2022 law.
sl.why: The framework establishes a mechanism to monitor government compliance with gender equality legislation.

sl.headline: President Bio warns against sale of Kush drug
sl.body: President Julius Maada Bio called on dealers to stop selling the synthetic drug known as Kush during a visit to the Government’s Harmful Drug Rehabilitation Facility in Hastings on October 30, 2025. The president stated that some parents are selling the substance.
sl.why: The crackdown aims to reduce the illicit trade of synthetic drugs that the president says is wreaking havoc in the country.

sl.headline: Freetown to rebuild King Jimmy market into modern indoor facility
sl.body: The King Jimmy market, one of West Africa's oldest markets established during the slave trade, will be rebuilt as a modern indoor market. The project involves a complete reconstruction of the historic site.
sl.why: The redevelopment replaces an open-air historic site with modern infrastructure for vendors and shoppers.

so.headline: Al-Shabaab attacks in Mogadishu fall from 144 to 5
so.body: Recorded attacks by Al-Shabaab in Mogadishu declined from 144 to 5. The figures are cited in a new report by The Economist.
so.why: The reduction in violence changes the security landscape for residents and businesses operating in the capital.

so.headline: Somali pirates demand $3 million for 10 Pakistani sailors
so.body: Pirates have requested $3 million to release 10 Pakistani sailors held since April. A Pakistani minister reported the demand on Wednesday following the hijacking of an oil tanker.
so.why: The demand creates a financial burden for the sailors' employers or the Pakistani government to secure their release.

so.headline: Somalia postpones Hirshabelle parliamentary and local elections
so.body: The Independent National Electoral and Boundaries Commission postponed elections for local councils and the House of Representatives in Hirshabelle state. The polls were scheduled for Thursday, Aug. 20.
so.why: The delay prevents the immediate seating of new representatives and local officials in the state.

so.headline: Former Somali president blames government for 30 deaths in Baidoa
so.body: Former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed attributed 30 deaths during fighting in Baidoa to the federal government of President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. Sharif stated on Tuesday that the violence resulted from a change of power imposed by force in Southwest State in March.
so.why: The accusation escalates political tension between the former president and the current federal administration.

so.headline: Pirates hijack cargo ship carrying Turkish weapons
so.body: Pirates hijacked a Cameroonian-flagged cargo ship and captured its 10-member crew earlier this week. A Somali official said the vessel and its cargo were taken toward the Nugaal coast.
so.why: The seizure of weapons cargo increases the risk of illicit arms entering the Puntland region.

ss.headline: Violence at Bentiu IDP camp kills 9
ss.body: At least nine people were killed and 23 others wounded during violence at the Bentiu internally displaced persons camp in Unity State. Sudans Post reports the clashes began when authorities attempted to arrest a self-proclaimed prophet named Taban Puol.
ss.why: The unrest disrupts the safety of displaced populations in Unity State.

ss.headline: IRC delivers health and education facilities in Aweil South
ss.body: The International Rescue Committee handed over two renovated primary schools and health facilities to authorities in Aweil South County. Sudans Post reports the project was funded by the World Bank.
ss.why: The new facilities increase local community access to essential medical and educational services.

ss.headline: Nyangwara community seeks halt to Nyamini land demarcation
ss.body: The Nyangwara-Pojulu-Tijor community has called for a stop to land allocation and demarcation in Juba County. Eye Radio reports the dispute over the land has lasted more than 13 years.
ss.why: The ongoing conflict prevents the legal resolution of competing land claims for residents in Nyamini.

ss.headline: Governor Adil vows crackdown on illegal mining
ss.body: Central Equatoria State Governor Emmanuel Adil Anthony announced a crackdown on illegal mining and armed groups. Radio Tamazuj reports the measure was announced Thursday.
ss.why: The initiative aims to curb unauthorized extraction of mineral resources within the state.

ss.headline: Former finance minister Kosti Manibe dies
ss.body: Former finance minister Kosti Manibe Ngai died on August 11, 2026. Sudans Post reports the death was acknowledged by RJMEC Chairperson Maj. Gen. George Aggrey Owinow.
ss.why: The loss removes a veteran politician involved in the country's peace process and public service.

sd.headline: Sudan army gains 318 RSF defectors
sd.body: The Sudanese army reports that 318 Rapid Support Forces fighters, including four commanders, have defected to its ranks. The army stated the move comes as fighting continues more than three years into the war.
sd.why: The surrender of paramilitary personnel reduces the manpower of the RSF during the ongoing conflict.

sd.headline: IOM reports 200,000 displaced in Kordofan
sd.body: More than 200,000 people have been displaced across Sudan's Kordofan region. The International Organization for Migration attributed the movement to intensifying fighting.
sd.why: The mass movement of civilians disrupts local stability and increases the need for humanitarian aid in the region.

sd.headline: UN records 14,000 displaced in Blue Nile state
sd.body: Nearly 14,000 people were displaced in August in Sudan's Blue Nile state. The UN migration agency cited rising tensions and clashes in Qaisan and Kurmuk.
sd.why: Worsening security in these specific districts forces residents to abandon their homes.

sd.headline: RSF attacks displace 1,000 in North Kordofan
sd.body: Attacks on two villages southwest of the North Kordofan capital killed six people and displaced more than 1,000 residents. The Sudan Tribune reports 215 families arrived on foot.
sd.why: The violence forces rural families to flee their villages and travel on foot to seek safety.

sd.headline: Khartoum students return to schools amid war
sd.body: Children in Khartoum are returning to classrooms as security improves. Africanews reports that schools remain damaged and suffer from a shortage of teachers and supplies.
sd.why: Overcrowded classes and lack of materials hinder the quality of education for returning students.

tg.headline: Togo reports 2,244.31 billion FCFA in domestic debt
tg.body: Togo's domestic debt stands at 2,244.31 billion FCFA. The figure was discussed during a July 30 meeting in Lomé between public and private sector actors. The session aimed to identify constraints hindering private sector growth.
tg.why: High levels of domestic debt limit the availability of credit and investment for local businesses.

tg.headline: Togo grants provisional release to one French journalist
tg.body: One of two French journalists arrested on July 27 in Kara was granted provisional release on August 20. The journalists and their local fixer were indicted on August 17. A judge in Lomé presided over the hearing.
tg.why: The release follows charges of 'false declarations' and a dispute over whether the crew had proper accreditation to film.

tg.headline: Togo Senate opens second extraordinary session of 2026
tg.body: The Togolese Senate began its second extraordinary session of the year on August 17. The session was convened at the request of President Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé. Meetings are being held at the Palais des Congrès in Lomé.
tg.why: The session allows the Senate to address specific legislative priorities requested by the presidency outside of regular calendar dates.

tg.headline: Togo hospital practitioners union launches 'Organizing' project
tg.body: The National Union of Hospital Practitioners of Togo (SYNPHOT) launched a project called 'Organizing' on August 17. The initiative was introduced during an event in Lomé. The project seeks to increase unionization among health professionals.
tg.why: Increased union membership gives healthcare workers more collective bargaining power regarding working conditions and pay.

tn.headline: Tunisia records 1,101 protests in July
tn.body: Tunisia saw 1,101 protest movements in July 2026, the highest monthly level since July 2016. The Tunisian Social Observatory reported that more than 60% of these mobilizations were related to specific problems.
tn.why: The surge in unrest indicates a record level of social instability for the country in a decade.

tn.headline: Tunisia opens online school registrations for 2026-2027
tn.body: The Ministry of Education opened remote registration and re-registration for primary, preparatory, and secondary students on Thursday, Aug. 20, starting at 8 p.m. The process is conducted online.
tn.why: Parents must now use a digital platform to secure their children's placement for the upcoming academic year.

tn.headline: Black Sea tensions pressure Tunisian wheat imports
tn.body: Tunisia remains dependent on imported wheat despite a strong domestic cereal campaign. Attacks on ships and ports in the Black Sea are disrupting one of the world's primary grain basins, according to Webdo.
tn.why: Supply chain disruptions in the Black Sea increase the risk of grain shortages for Tunisian consumers.

tn.headline: Tunis medina schedules Mouled procession for Aug. 25
tn.body: A large procession will start at 9:30 a.m. on Tuesday, Aug. 25, at the zaouia of Sidi Mahrez. The event will move through the Tunis medina toward the zaouia of Sidi Ben Arous.
tn.why: The event closes or restricts movement on the rue du Pacha for the duration of the religious festivities.

tn.headline: Tunisian government reviews 2027 economic balance
tn.body: Prime Minister Sara Zaafrani Zenzri presided over a ministerial council on Wednesday, Aug. 19, to examine the draft economic balance for 2027. The document serves as the major orientation for the country's economic policy.
tn.why: The resulting balance will determine the allocation of state funds and fiscal priorities for the 2027 budget year.

zm.headline: Police confirm former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya killed in security raid
zm.body: Police confirmed the death of former Minister of Works and Transport Mutotwe Kafwaya. The death occurred during a security raid on an opposition media outlet, according to BBC Africa.
zm.why: The killing of a former government official during a raid on a media house increases pressure on national security authorities.

zm.headline: Opposition leader Brian Mundubile challenges presidential poll results
zm.body: Opposition leader Brian Mundubile is challenging the results of the presidential election in court. Mundubile alleges his campaign documented serious irregularities in the counting and transmission of votes, Africanews reports.
zm.why: The legal challenge contests the legitimacy of the current administration's mandate following the August elections.

zm.headline: US and Serbia congratulate President-elect Hakainde Hichilema
zm.body: The United States and Serbia have issued statements congratulating Hakainde Hichilema on his re-election. The two nations pledged to strengthen bilateral relations and cooperation, according to the Lusaka Times.
zm.why: These diplomatic recognitions signal continued international support and cooperation for Hichilema's second term.

zm.headline: Zambia copper boom attracts billions in green-energy investment
zm.body: Zambia's copper sector is attracting billions in green-energy investment. Africanews reports the boom occurs as the neighboring DRC implements a copper and cobalt export ban to target refining margins.
zm.why: The influx of capital targets the mining sector, though citizens are questioning the distribution of these financial benefits.

zm.headline: Police probe death of 25-year-old Lisa Mutambo
zm.body: Police are investigating the death of 25-year-old Lisa Mutambo, who was brought to a hospital dead on August 20. Deputy Police Public Relations Officer Chipo Kaitisha stated that no physical injuries were found on the body.
zm.why: The official police finding of no physical injuries contradicts social media reports alleging the woman was beaten to death.

eh.headline: VOX MEP proposes ceding Western Sahara to Morocco
eh.body: European Parliament member Hermann Tertsch proposed accepting Moroccan claims over Western Sahara in exchange for Rabat recognizing Spanish sovereignty over Ceuta and Melilla. The proposal was detailed in a public message. The VOX party has not publicly disavowed the statements.
eh.why: The proposal suggests a territorial exchange that would change the legal status of Western Sahara to secure the status of Spanish exclaves.

eh.headline: Morocco threatens to review Spanish contracts over World Cup boycott
eh.body: Rabat warned it could review future contracts with Spanish companies if political pressure continues to exclude Morocco from the 2030 World Cup. The warning was reported by Moroccan media. Morocco is co-hosting the tournament with Spain and Portugal.
eh.why: Spanish firms face potential loss of contracts if political opposition to the World Cup organization persists.

eh.headline: Tens of thousands enter Ceuta from Morocco
eh.body: Tens of thousands of people entered Ceuta from Morocco in late July 2026. Sahrawi diplomat Jadiyetu El Mohtar described the event as a crisis. The incident highlighted European security dependence on Morocco.
eh.why: The mass entry of people creates an immediate security and humanitarian challenge for European authorities in the enclave.

eh.headline: Declassified US cable links Juan Carlos I to Melilla cession talks
eh.body: A 1979 US diplomatic document released by WikiLeaks indicates King Juan Carlos I considered ceding Melilla to Morocco. The cable describes conversations regarding formulas to resolve the future of Ceuta and Melilla. The document was recently declassified.
eh.why: The disclosure reveals historical royal willingness to negotiate the transfer of Spanish territory to Morocco.

ls.headline: Auditor-General cites M30 million budget shortfall
ls.body: The Office of the Auditor-General (OAG) reported a M30 million budget allocation for the 2026/27 financial year is insufficient. The OAG testified before the parliamentary Economic and Development Cluster Committee this week.
ls.why: The funding gap has left the institution struggling with mounting debts.

ls.headline: LAA and LHDA settle ground rent dispute for M121 million
ls.body: The Land Administration Authority and the Lesotho Highlands Development Authority agreed to a M121 million settlement. The agreement was presented before Chief Justice Sakoane Sakoane.
ls.why: The payment resolves a long-running dispute over unpaid ground rent between the two entities.

ls.headline: Auditor-General spends M12 million on LEC forensic audit
ls.body: The Office of the Auditor-General spent M12 million on a forensic audit of the Lesotho Electricity Company. The expenditure was disclosed during a review by the Economic and Development Cluster this week.
ls.why: The audit aims to investigate financial mismanagement, procurement irregularities, and other alleged wrongdoing at the utility.

ls.headline: Police sued for M3.2 million over alleged torture
ls.body: Retired government employee Molebatsi Monese is suing Chief Police Advocate Borotho Matsoso for M3.2 million. The lawsuit filed in the High Court alleges Monese was suffocated, electrocuted, and had two teeth knocked out during interrogation.
ls.why: The legal action seeks damages for torture allegedly inflicted by police officers.

ls.headline: Businesswoman sues Lesotho Defence Force for M6 million
ls.body: A Maseru businesswoman is suing the Lesotho Defence Force and Lieutenant General Mojalefa Letsoela for more than M6 million. The claim relates to an unpaid balance for military jerseys supplied over a decade ago.
ls.why: The plaintiff claims the army's failure to settle the debt crippled her business.
